skill.name: datadog-automation
skill.description: Automate Datadog metrics, logs, monitors, dashboards, events, downtimes, hosts, and traces through Rube MCP with schema-first workflows.
skill.summary: Use Rube MCP to run common Datadog observability workflows from AI coding tools.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static command-execution and system-reconnaissance findings are false positives from Markdown inline code, Datadog query examples, and tool names. The skill does direct users to a third-party MCP endpoint and supports Datadog operations that can change or suppress monitoring, so permission and confirmation controls are required.

remediation.issue: Third-party MCP endpoint and Datadog authentication
remediation.suggestion: Document Rube MCP data access, Datadog auth scopes, and approval requirements before users connect production Datadog accounts.
Require explicit confirmation for dashboard deletion, monitor updates, monitor muting, and downtimes, including resource identifiers and end times.

remediation.issue: Broad observability reads can expose sensitive operational data
remediation.suggestion: Recommend least-privilege Datadog roles, narrow time ranges, and redaction of sensitive log fields before returning results.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Datadog connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `datadog`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
- Query syntax follows Datadog's metric query format: `aggregation:metric_name{tag_filters}`
- `from` and `to` are Unix epoch timestamps in seconds, not milliseconds
2. `DATADOG_SEARCH_LOGS` - Search logs with query and filters [Required]
- `query`: Log search query using Datadog log query syntax
- `limit`: Number of log entries to return
- Log queries use Datadog's log search syntax: `service:web status:error`
- `type`: Monitor type ('metric alert', 'service check', 'log alert', 'query alert', etc.)
- `query`: Monitor query defining the alert condition
- Monitor `type` must match the query type; mismatches cause creation failures
- Thresholds vary by monitor type; metric monitors need `critical` at minimum
- `layout_type` cannot be changed after creation; must recreate the dashboard
- `end`: End time (Unix epoch; omit for indefinite)
- `monitor_id`: Specific monitor to downtime (optional, omit for scope-based)
- Event `text` supports Datadog's markdown format including @mentions
- Omitting `end` creates an indefinite downtime; always set an end time for maintenance
- Downtime `monitor_id` narrows to a single monitor; scope applies to all matching monitors
- `trace_id`: Distributed trace ID for trace lookup
- Use `page` and `page_size` or offset-based pagination depending on endpoint
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k

content.value_statement: Datadog work often requires switching between metrics, logs, monitors, dashboards, and incident context. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a schema-first workflow for common Datadog automation through Rube MCP.
actual_capabilities: Search current Rube MCP Datadog tools before using tool schemas.
Query Datadog metrics and list available metric names.
Search Datadog logs and list log indexes for investigation workflows.
List, inspect, create, update, mute, and unmute Datadog monitors.
List, inspect, update, and delete Datadog dashboards.
Create Datadog events, schedule downtimes, list hosts, and inspect traces.
limitations: Requires an active Rube MCP server and an authenticated Datadog connection.
Cannot validate changes against your internal approval process without explicit instructions.
Destructive actions depend on the permissions granted to the connected Datadog account.
Tool schemas may change, so the skill instructs users to search current tools first.

use_cases.title: Investigate Production Alerts
use_cases.description: Query metrics, search related logs, and inspect monitor details from one guided workflow.

use_cases.title: Maintain Observability Assets
use_cases.description: Review dashboard definitions and make controlled Datadog updates with current tool schemas.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Maintenance Windows
use_cases.description: Create events or scheduled downtimes while keeping scope and end times explicit.

prompt_templates.title: List Relevant Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Datadog automation skill to list available metrics related to the production api service.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Error Logs
prompt_templates.prompt: Search recent Datadog logs for production errors in the web service, then summarize patterns and likely follow-up checks.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Monitor Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Find existing CPU monitors, inspect one similar monitor, and draft a new monitor plan for the production host group.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Safe Maintenance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review affected monitors and dashboards for the checkout service, then prepare a bounded downtime plan with scope and rollback checks.

output_examples.input: Investigate production latency for the checkout service during the last hour.
output_examples.output: A concise incident summary with metric trends, related log patterns, affected services, and recommended Datadog follow-up checks.

output_examples.input: Prepare a dashboard update for the payments team.
output_examples.output: A change plan listing the current dashboard state, proposed widget updates, validation steps, and confirmation points before applying changes.

output_examples.input: Schedule maintenance downtime for staging hosts tonight.
output_examples.output: A scoped downtime plan with target tags, start and end times, affected monitors, and a reminder to confirm Datadog permissions.

best_practices: Search current Rube MCP tool schemas before every Datadog workflow.
Use least-privilege Datadog roles and confirm every write or delete action.
Set explicit time ranges, scopes, and downtime end times before running operations.
anti_patterns: Do not delete dashboards or mute monitors without explicit user confirmation.
Do not request broad log exports when a narrow time range and service filter will work.
Do not treat Datadog output as a replacement for incident review or change approval.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It guides Datadog workflows for metrics, logs, monitors, dashboards, events, downtimes, hosts, and traces through Rube MCP.

faq.question: Does it require a Datadog account?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires an authenticated Datadog connection through Rube MCP before Datadog tools can run.

faq.question: Can it change production monitors?
faq.answer: Yes, if the connected Datadog account has permission. Users should require explicit confirmation for every write action.

faq.question: Can it delete dashboards?
faq.answer: The skill documents a dashboard delete workflow. Treat deletion as irreversible and require a clear approval step.

faq.question: Why does it search tools first?
faq.answer: Rube MCP tool schemas can change. Searching first helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use current parameters.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for Datadog expertise?
faq.answer: No. It helps run workflows, but users still need environment knowledge, permissions, and operational review.
